_comment: Sister Oriel Vane, 29, a Dawn Throne healer who left Envoy Lucan's train. Found in the Ashford healer's lot. Flags: docs/regions/COMPANIONS_R1.md.

lines.text: Sit. Whatever it is, it's worse when you stand on it.
Dawn comes whether anyone asks it to. I used to find that comforting.
Keep the bandages dry and the questions short. I will do the rest.
It went back to the sun, and the sun did not object. I am still not sure it ought to have been asked.
It sleeps in your stone now. I check on it. Humour me; healers fuss.
You look tired. Come here. No, I mean it, I will check your pulse and nothing else. Tonight.
Friends. Gladly. I have too few I can tell the truth to.

choices.text: Come with me. We need a healer.
What did you carry out of Lucan's train?

lines.text: Oriel Vane, Sister of the Morning Watch. Healer. Twenty-nine. I came east with Envoy Lucan to bless wells.
Then I was told to burn a lamp at a roadside shrine. A lantern with an ember in it. Our own order's, two centuries old.
Because the Church calls embers heathen, and I was holding one in my hands. It was warm. It knew me. I could not.

choices.text: Come with me. We need a healer.

lines.text: Terms: no wage, a tenth of whatever you earn, and I choose who I heal first. Even the ones you would not.
Then I walk with you. Do not ask me to curse the Envoy. He is a good man being lied to by his own faith.
Take what time you need. I will be here, mending, and arguing with the sun.
I left the lamp in a milestone on the King's Ember Road. I should go back for it. I should not go alone.
Lucan will ask where it is. Tell him, or do not. Either way I will not tell you which to choose.
You have not once asked me to be braver than I am. I have noticed. It is rarer than sunrise.

choices.text: I'd like that. As Oriel, not Sister.

lines.text: Slowly, then. I am a healer. I know what happens when you rush the stitching.
Gladly. Truly. Go on, then. Say it is a good idea.
A small brass lantern, ember-bright. Our order took it from a village that would not give it up.
A midwife called Idony. The label says Saint. The ember says she asked them, very politely, to stop.

choices.text: We will do right by her.
